messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Forty years ago, during an early autumn harvest, Amara Jenkins was working past the eastern treeline when the shadow detached itself from the soybean rows. The violation lasted hours, but what etched itself into her nervous system was the sudden, suffocating silence that followed—no crickets, no wind, just the flat quiet of a landscape holding its breath—and the thick, loamy scent of overturned earth clinging to her skin. When she finally dragged herself home, the soil smell followed her into every room, a permanent marker of what had been done to her in the dark. As the years passed, that single September night colonized her present. Every October, when the calendar turned to the anniversary, the air would grow heavy, and the mere whisper of dirt under her boots would pull her back to the field. She began to equate the ground itself with violation; the rich black soil that fed her livelihood now smelled of loss. In her mind, the contamination seeped inward. She could scrub until her knuckles cracked, but the feeling of being permanently soiled never left. That sense of defilement warred with a deeper conviction: that a body used so roughly, stained so thoroughly, could never hold value again. She started questioning whether any of the years she had gathered were enough to justify continuing. To survive the weight of those thoughts, Amara built walls of silence and repetition. When the yardage sounds outside the barn suddenly died down, forcing her back toward the field, she immediately retreated to the house and refused any physical contact from her husband. The sensory trigger demanded escape, but the sudden silence alone was enough to convince her that the contamination seeped inward, reinforcing the conviction that she could never truly be clean. Believing herself fundamentally defiled, she forced herself to catalog every small blessing in the day, counting harvest bonuses and garden yields until her mind stopped spiraling. The positive reframing was meant to be a shield, but the mental effort only reminded her how corrupted she felt, which in turn made the scent of fresh tilled earth impossible to ignore. Avoidance of the dusk light kept the dark at bay, yet by refusing to engage with it, she taught her nervous system that silence was a threat worth bracing for. Each strategy she deployed to feel safe only sharpened the memory of the soil and solidified the belief that her life had lost its anchor, turning every quiet evening into a waiting room for shame. The avoidance became a quiet erosion of her days. She stopped walking the property line with her partner, claiming her knees could no longer handle the uneven ground, which left him reaching out across the breakfast table to no avail. Her work in the crops narrowed to sunlit mornings, and she hired a seasonal hand to manage the evening irrigation, paying a premium just to keep her boots from touching the dew-heavy rows after sundown. The isolation compounded over decades. By the time she reached seventy-four, the positive thoughts no longer stuck, the avoidance left her utterly alone, and the shame felt too heavy to carry into winter. She has come to seek counseling not because she wants to relive the field, but because she fears the relationship will fracture completely without intervention. She hopes, despite her certainty, that someone might help her untangle the knot without forcing her back into the dirt.
